sanskrit: mumūrṣur hi naraḥ sarvān vṛkṣān paśyati kāñcanān tathā tvam api gāndhāre viparītāni paśyasi
english: For a man about to die sees all the trees as turned to gold; even so do you, O son of Gāndhārī, behold all things inverted.

sanskrit: svayaṃ vairaṃ mahat kṛtvā pāṇḍavaiḥ sahasṛñjayaiḥ yudhyasva tān adya raṇe paśyāmaḥ puruṣo bhava
english: Having yourself kindled this great enmity with the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas, fight them now in battle. Let us watch—be a man!

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu somakān sarvān sapāñcālān samāgatān nihaniṣye naravyāghra varjayitvā śikhaṇḍinam
english: As for me, O tiger among men, I shall slay all the Somakas and the Pāñcālas who are gathered here, sparing only Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: tair vāhaṃ nihataḥ saṃkhye gamiṣye yamasādanam tān vā nihatya saṃgrāme prītiṃ dāsyāmi vai tava
english: Either slain by them in battle I shall go to the abode of Yama, or, having slain them in the fray, I shall give you joy.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ hi strī samutpannā śikhaṇḍī rājaveśmani varadānāt pumāñ jātaḥ saiṣā vai strī śikhaṇḍinī
english: For Śikhaṇḍin was born a woman at first within the royal house; by the boon she became a man—yet she is still that woman, Śikhaṇḍinī.

sanskrit: tām ahaṃ na haniṣyāmi prāṇatyāge 'pi bhārata yāsau prāṅ nirmitā dhātrā saiṣā vai strī śikhaṇḍinī
english: Her I shall not slay, O Bhārata, even at the cost of my own life; she whom the Creator first fashioned thus is verily that woman, Śikhaṇḍinī.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ svapihi gāndhāre śvo 'smi kartā mahāraṇam yaj janāḥ kathayiṣyanti yāvat sthāsyati medinī
english: Sleep at ease, O son of Gāndhārī; tomorrow I shall wage such a great battle as men will recount for as long as the earth endures.

sanskrit: evam uktas tava suto nirjagāma janeśvara abhivādya guruṃ mūrdhnā prayayau svaṃ niveśanam
english: Thus addressed, O lord of men, your son departed; bowing his head in reverence to the elder, he went away to his own dwelling.

sanskrit: āgamya tu tato rājā visṛjya ca mahājanam praviveśa tatas tūrṇaṃ kṣayaṃ śatrukṣayaṃkaraḥ praviṣṭaḥ sa niśāṃ tāṃ ca gamayām āsa pārthivaḥ
english: Having come there, the king dismissed the great throng, and that bringer of doom to his foes swiftly entered his lodging; and so entered, the prince passed that night away.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ prātar utthāya vai nṛpaḥ rājñaḥ samājñāpayata senāṃ yojayateti ha adya bhīṣmo raṇe kruddho nihaniṣyati somakān
english: Saṃjaya said: When the night had brightened into dawn, the king rose at morning and commanded the kings, "Array the army! Today Bhīṣma, wrathful in battle, shall slay the Somakas."

sanskrit: duryodhanasya tac chrutvā rātrau vilapitaṃ bahu manyamānaḥ sa taṃ rājan pratyādeśam ivātmanaḥ
english: Bhīṣma, hearing all of Duryodhana's lament uttered in the night, O king, regarded it as a rebuke directed against himself.

sanskrit: nirvedaṃ paramaṃ gatvā vinindya paravācyatām dīrghaṃ dadhyau śāṃtanavo yoddhukāmo 'rjunaṃ raṇe
english: Falling into utter despondency, censuring the slander of others, the son of Śaṃtanu brooded long, eager to do battle with Arjuna in the field.

sanskrit: iṅgitena tu taj jñātvā gāṅgeyena vicintitam duryodhano mahārāja duḥśāsanam acodayat
english: Discerning by signs what the son of Gaṅgā was pondering, Duryodhana, O great king, urged on Duḥśāsana.

sanskrit: duḥśāsana rathās tūrṇaṃ yujyantāṃ bhīṣmarakṣiṇaḥ dvātriṃśat tvam anīkāni sarvāṇy evābhicodaya
english: "Duḥśāsana, let the chariots that guard Bhīṣma be yoked at once, and urge forward all the two-and-thirty divisions."

sanskrit: idaṃ hi samanuprāptaṃ varṣapūgābhicintitam pāṇḍavānāṃ sasainyānāṃ vadho rājyasya cāgamaḥ
english: "For now is at hand that which we have pondered through many years: the slaughter of the Pāṇḍavas with their hosts, and the winning of the kingdom."

sanskrit: tatra kāryam ahaṃ manye bhīṣmasyaivābhirakṣaṇam sa no guptaḥ sukhāya syād dhanyāt pārthāṃś ca saṃyuge
english: "In this I deem the protection of Bhīṣma to be the chief task; guarded by us he would bring us comfort, and would slay the sons of Pṛthā in the fray."

sanskrit: abravīc ca viśuddhātmā nāhaṃ hanyāṃ śikhaṇḍinam strīpūrvako hy asau jātas tasmād varjyo raṇe mayā
english: "And that pure-souled one declared, 'I will not slay Śikhaṇḍin, for he was born a woman before; therefore he must be spared by me in battle.'"

sanskrit: lokas tad veda yad ahaṃ pituḥ priyacikīrṣayā rājyaṃ sphītaṃ mahābāho striyaś ca tyaktavān purā
english: "'The world knows this—that I, O mighty-armed one, to do my father's pleasure, of old renounced a flourishing kingdom and the company of women.'"

sanskrit: naiva cāhaṃ striyaṃ jātu na strīpūrvaṃ kathaṃ cana hanyāṃ yudhi naraśreṣṭha satyam etad bravīmi te
english: "'Never in any wise would I slay a woman, nor one who was a woman before, in battle, O best of men; this truth I tell you.'"

sanskrit: ayaṃ strīpūrvako rājañ śikhaṇḍī yadi te śrutaḥ udyoge kathitaṃ yat tat tathā jātā śikhaṇḍinī
english: "'This Śikhaṇḍin, O king, was a woman before, if you have heard the tale told in the Udyoga—even so was Śikhaṇḍinī born.'"

sanskrit: kanyā bhūtvā pumāñ jātaḥ sa ca yotsyati bhārata tasyāhaṃ pramukhe bāṇān na muñceyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: "'Having been a maiden, she was born a man, and he shall fight, O Bhārata; yet against his face I would in no way loose my arrows.'"

sanskrit: yuddhe tu kṣatriyāṃs tāta pāṇḍavānāṃ jayaiṣiṇaḥ sarvān anyān haniṣyāmi saṃprāptān bāṇagocarān
english: "'But all the other Kṣatriyas, dear one, who seek the Pāṇḍavas' victory and come within range of my arrows, I shall slay in battle.'"

sanskrit: evaṃ māṃ bharataśreṣṭho gāṅgeyaḥ prāha śāstravit tatra sarvātmanā manye bhīṣmasyaivābhipālanam
english: "Thus did the son of Gaṅgā, best of the Bhāratas, knower of the scriptures, speak to me; therefore I deem the guarding of Bhīṣma to be our whole concern."

sanskrit: arakṣyamāṇaṃ hi vṛko hanyāt siṃhaṃ mahāvane mā vṛkeṇeva śārdūlaṃ ghātayema śikhaṇḍinā
english: "For a wolf, if the lion be left unguarded, might slay the lion in the great forest; let us not, as it were by a wolf, let the tiger be slain by Śikhaṇḍin."

sanskrit: mātulaḥ śakuniḥ śalyaḥ kṛpo droṇo viviṃśatiḥ yattā rakṣantu gāṅgeyaṃ tasmin gupte dhruvo jayaḥ
english: "Let my uncle Śakuni, and Śalya, Kṛpa, Droṇa, and Viviṃśati, vigilant, guard the son of Gaṅgā; when he is protected, victory is sure."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu rājāno duryodhanavacas tadā sarvato rathavaṃśena gāṅgeyaṃ paryavārayan
english: Hearing this speech of Duryodhana, the kings then surrounded the son of Gaṅgā on every side with a host of chariots.

sanskrit: putrāś ca tava gāṅgeyaṃ parivārya yayur mudā kampayanto bhuvaṃ dyāṃ ca kṣobhayantaś ca pāṇḍavān
english: And your sons, encircling the son of Gaṅgā, advanced with joy, making the earth and sky to tremble and throwing the Pāṇḍavas into confusion.

sanskrit: tai rathaiś ca susaṃyuktair dantibhiś ca mahārathāḥ parivārya raṇe bhīṣmaṃ daṃśitāḥ samavasthitāḥ
english: With those well-yoked chariots and with elephants, the great warriors, mailed for battle, encircled Bhīṣma and took their stand.

sanskrit: yathā devāsure yuddhe tridaśā vajradhāriṇam sarve te sma vyatiṣṭhanta rakṣantas taṃ mahāratham
english: As in the war of gods and demons the thirty surrounded the Wielder of the Thunderbolt, so did they all stand guarding that mighty warrior.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā punar bhrātaram abravīt savyaṃ cakraṃ yudhāmanyur uttamaujāś ca dakṣiṇam goptārāv arjunasyaitāv arjuno 'pi śikhaṇḍinaḥ
english: Then king Duryodhana spoke again to his brother: "Yudhāmanyu guards Arjuna's left wheel and Uttamaujas his right; these two are Arjuna's protectors, and Arjuna in turn is Śikhaṇḍin's."

sanskrit: sa rakṣyamāṇaḥ pārthena tathāsmābhir vivarjitaḥ yathā bhīṣmaṃ na no hanyād duḥśāsana tathā kuru
english: "Though guarded by Pārtha and thus shunned by us, see to it, O Duḥśāsana, that he—Śikhaṇḍin—does not slay our Bhīṣma."

sanskrit: bhrātus tad vacanaṃ śrutvā putro duḥśāsanas tava bhīṣmaṃ pramukhataḥ kṛtvā prayayau senayā saha
english: Hearing his brother's words, your son Duḥśāsana, placing Bhīṣma at the forefront, advanced together with the army.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaṃ tu rathavaṃśena dṛṣṭvā tam abhisaṃvṛtam arjuno rathināṃ śreṣṭho dhṛṣṭadyumnam uvāca ha
english: But Arjuna, foremost of chariot-warriors, seeing Bhīṣma there encircled by that host of chariots, spoke thus to Dhṛṣṭadyumna:

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ naravyāghra bhīṣmasya pramukhe 'nagha sthāpayasvādya pāñcālya tasya goptāham apy uta
english: "O tiger among men, O sinless prince of the Pāñcālas, station Śikhaṇḍin this day at the very front, facing Bhīṣma; and I shall be his guardian."

sanskrit: tataḥ śāṃtanavo bhīṣmo niryayau senayā saha vyūhaṃ cāvyūhata mahat sarvatobhadram āhave
english: Then Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu, sallied forth with the army, and arrayed for the battle a great formation, the Sarvatobhadra, facing on every side.

sanskrit: kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca śaibyaś caiva mahārathaḥ śakuniḥ saindhavaś caiva kāmbojaś ca sudakṣiṇaḥ
english: Kṛpa and Kṛtavarman, and the great warrior of the Śaibyas, Śakuni and the lord of the Sindhus, and Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja—

sanskrit: bhīṣmeṇa sahitāḥ sarve putraiś ca tava bhārata agrataḥ sarvasainyānāṃ vyūhasya pramukhe sthitāḥ
english: all these, together with Bhīṣma and your sons, O Bhārata, took their stand in front of all the troops, at the head of the formation.

sanskrit: droṇo bhūriśravāḥ śalyo bhagadattaś ca māriṣa dakṣiṇaṃ pakṣam āśritya sthitā vyūhasya daṃśitāḥ
english: Droṇa, Bhūriśravas, Śalya, and Bhagadatta, O venerable one, mailed for war, took post upon the right wing of the formation.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā somadatta āvantyau ca mahārathau mahatyā senayā yuktā vāmaṃ pakṣam apālayan
english: Aśvatthāman, Somadatta, and the two great warriors of Avanti, joined by a mighty host, held the left wing.

sanskrit: duryodhano mahārāja trigartaiḥ sarvato vṛtaḥ vyūhamadhye sthito rājan pāṇḍavān prati bhārata
english: Duryodhana, O great king, surrounded on all sides by the Trigartas, stood in the midst of the formation, facing the Pāṇḍavas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: alambuso rathaśreṣṭhaḥ śrutāyuś ca mahārathaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sarvasainyānāṃ sthitau vyūhasya daṃśitau
english: Alambusa, foremost of chariot-warriors, and the great warrior Śrutāyus, both clad in mail, took their stand at the rear of all the troops, behind the formation.

sanskrit: evam ete tadā vyūhaṃ kṛtvā bhārata tāvakāḥ saṃnaddhāḥ samadṛśyanta pratapanta ivāgnayaḥ
english: Having thus drawn up their array, O Bhārata, your warriors, fully armed, appeared like blazing fires.

sanskrit: tathā yudhiṣṭhiro rājā bhīmasenaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca mādrīputrāv ubhāv api agrataḥ sarvasainyānāṃ sthitā vyūhasya daṃśitāḥ
english: In like manner king Yudhiṣṭhira and the Pāṇḍava Bhīmasena, and Nakula and Sahadeva, the two sons of Mādrī, mailed for war, took their stand in front of all the troops, at the head of the formation.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaś ca sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ sthitāḥ sainyena mahatā parānīkavināśanāḥ
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Virāṭa, and the great warrior Sātyaki, destroyers of the enemy's ranks, stood with a mighty host.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī vijayaś caiva rākṣasaś ca ghaṭotkacaḥ cekitāno mahābāhuḥ kuntibhojaś ca vīryavān sthitā raṇe mahārāja mahatyā senayā vṛtāḥ
english: Śikhaṇḍin and Vijaya, and the Rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca, the mighty-armed Cekitāna and the valiant Kuntibhoja, took their stand in the battle, O great king, encompassed by a mighty host.

sanskrit: abhimanyur maheṣvāso drupadaś ca mahārathaḥ kekayā bhrātaraḥ pañca sthitā yuddhāya daṃśitāḥ
english: Abhimanyu the great archer, and the mighty warrior Drupada, and the five Kekaya brothers, stood arrayed in mail for battle.

sanskrit: evaṃ te 'pi mahāvyūhaṃ prativyūhya sudurjayam pāṇḍavāḥ samare śūrāḥ sthitā yuddhāya māriṣa
english: Thus too did the heroic Pāṇḍavas, having drawn up against them their great and well-nigh invincible array, stand ready for battle, O venerable one.

sanskrit: tāvakās tu raṇe yattāḥ sahasenā narādhipāḥ abhyudyayū raṇe pārthān bhīṣmaṃ kṛtvāgrato nṛpa
english: And your kings, vigilant in the field, together with their hosts, advanced against the sons of Pṛthā in battle, placing Bhīṣma at their head, O king.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavā rājan bhīmasenapurogamāḥ bhīṣmaṃ yuddhapariprepsuṃ saṃgrāme vijigīṣavaḥ
english: In like manner the Pāṇḍavas, O king, with Bhīmasena at their front, eager for victory in the fray, advanced against Bhīṣma, who longed to do battle.

sanskrit: kṣveḍāḥ kilikilāśabdān krakacān goviṣāṇikāḥ bherīmṛdaṅgapaṇavān nādayantaś ca puṣkarān pāṇḍavā abhyadhāvanta nadanto bhairavān ravān
english: Sounding their war-cries and shrill clamors, their krakacas and cow-horns, their kettledrums, tabors, and tom-toms, and their drum-faces, the Pāṇḍavas rushed forward, raising terrible roars.

sanskrit: bherīmṛdaṅgaśaṅkhānāṃ dundubhīnāṃ ca nisvanaiḥ utkruṣṭasiṃhanādaiś ca valgitaiś ca pṛthagvidhaiḥ
english: With the din of kettledrums, tabors, conches, and great war-drums, with lion-roars raised on high and prancings of many kinds—

sanskrit: vayaṃ pratinadantas tān abhyagacchāma satvarāḥ sahasaivābhisaṃkruddhās tadāsīt tumulaṃ mahat
english: we, answering them with our own clamor, advanced upon them in haste, all at once and full of wrath; and there arose a great tumult.

sanskrit: tato 'nyonyaṃ pradhāvantaḥ saṃprahāraṃ pracakrire tataḥ śabdena mahatā pracakampe vasuṃdharā
english: Then, rushing upon one another, they fell to the clash of arms; and at that mighty roar the earth trembled.

sanskrit: pakṣiṇaś ca mahāghoraṃ vyāharanto vibabhramuḥ saprabhaś coditaḥ sūryo niṣprabhaḥ samapadyata
english: The birds wheeled about, crying out most dreadfully; and the sun, though risen in splendor, grew dim of light.

sanskrit: vavuś ca tumulā vātāḥ śaṃsantaḥ sumahad bhayam ghorāś ca ghoranirhrādāḥ śivās tatra vavāśire vedayantyo mahārāja mahad vaiśasam āgatam
english: Tumultuous winds blew, foretelling some most terrible fear; and there the jackals, dread and dread-howling, set up their cries, O great king, announcing that a great carnage was come.

sanskrit: diśaḥ prajvalitā rājan pāṃsuvarṣaṃ papāta ca rudhireṇa samunmiśram asthivarṣaṃ tathaiva ca
english: The quarters of the sky blazed forth, O king, and a rain of dust fell down, and likewise a rain of bones mingled with blood.

sanskrit: rudatāṃ vāhanānāṃ ca netrebhyaḥ prāpataj jalam susruvuś ca śakṛnmūtraṃ pradhyāyanto viśāṃ pate
english: From the eyes of the weeping beasts of burden water fell, and they let flow their dung and urine, sunk in brooding, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: antarhitā mahānādāḥ śrūyante bharatarṣabha rakṣasāṃ puruṣādānāṃ nadatāṃ bhairavān ravān
english: Unseen, O bull of the Bhāratas, mighty cries were heard—the terrible roars of man-devouring Rākṣasas as they bellowed.

sanskrit: saṃpatantaḥ sma dṛśyante gomāyubakavāyasāḥ śvānaś ca vividhair nādair bhaṣantas tatra tasthire
english: Jackals, herons, and crows were seen flocking together; and dogs, barking with cries of many sorts, stood there about.

sanskrit: jvalitāś ca maholkā vai samāhatya divākaram nipetuḥ sahasā bhūmau vedayānā mahad bhayam
english: And great blazing meteors, striking against the sun, fell suddenly upon the earth, announcing some great terror.

sanskrit: mahānty anīkāni mahāsamucchraye; samāgame pāṇḍavadhārtarāṣṭrayoḥ prakāśire śaṅkhamṛdaṅganisvanaiḥ; prakampitānīva vanāni vāyunā
english: At that great uprising, in the meeting of the Pāṇḍavas and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the mighty armies shone forth with the blare of conches and tabors, like forests set atremble by the wind.

sanskrit: narendranāgāśvasamākulānām; abhyāyatīnām aśive muhūrte babhūva ghoṣas tumulaś camūnāṃ; vātoddhutānām iva sāgarāṇām
english: In that ill-boding hour, as the hosts—thronged with kings, elephants, and horses—came on, there arose a tumultuous roar of the armies, like that of oceans uplifted by the wind.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca abhimanyū rathodāraḥ piśaṅgais turagottamaiḥ abhidudrāva tejasvī duryodhanabalaṃ mahat vikirañ śaravarṣāṇi vāridhārā ivāmbudaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Abhimanyu, splendid upon his chariot, with his excellent tawny steeds, that fiery one, charged against the great host of Duryodhana, scattering showers of arrows as a raincloud scatters torrents of water.

sanskrit: na śekuḥ samare kruddhaṃ saubhadram arisūdanam śastraughiṇaṃ gāhamānaṃ senāsāgaram akṣayam nivārayitum apy ājau tvadīyāḥ kurupuṃgavāḥ
english: Your warriors, the bulls among the Kurus, could not even check in the battle the wrathful son of Subhadrā, that slayer of foes, as with his flood of weapons he plunged into the unfathomable ocean of the army.

sanskrit: tena muktā raṇe rājañ śarāḥ śatrunibarhaṇāḥ kṣatriyān anayañ śūrān pretarājaniveśanam
english: The shafts loosed by him in the battle, O king, crushers of foes, led heroic Kṣatriyas to the dwelling of the king of the dead.

sanskrit: yamadaṇḍopamān ghorāñ jvalanāśīviṣopamān saubhadraḥ samare kruddhaḥ preṣayām āsa sāyakān
english: Arrows dreadful as the rod of Yama, like blazing venomous serpents, did the son of Subhadrā, wrathful in the fray, send forth.

sanskrit: rathinaṃ ca rathāt tūrṇaṃ hayapṛṣṭhāc ca sādinam gajārohāṃś ca sagajān pātayām āsa phālguniḥ
english: The chariot-warrior from his car, the horseman from his horse's back, and the elephant-riders together with their elephants—all these did the son of Phalguna swiftly bring down.

sanskrit: tasya tat kurvataḥ karma mahat saṃkhye 'dbhutaṃ nṛpāḥ pūjayāṃ cakrire hṛṣṭāḥ praśaśaṃsuś ca phālgunim
english: As he wrought that great and wondrous deed in battle, the kings, rejoicing, did him honor and extolled the son of Phalguna.

sanskrit: tāny anīkāni saubhadro drāvayan bahv aśobhata tūlarāśim ivādhūya mārutaḥ sarvatodiśam
english: Routing those ranks, the son of Subhadrā shone exceedingly, like the wind that scatters a heap of cotton in every direction.

sanskrit: tena vidrāvyamāṇāni tava sainyāni bhārata trātāraṃ nādhyagacchanta paṅke magnā iva dvipāḥ
english: Driven in rout by him, your troops, O Bhārata, found no protector, like elephants sunk fast in the mire.

sanskrit: vidrāvya sarvasainyāni tāvakāni narottamaḥ abhimanyuḥ sthito rājan vidhūmo 'gnir iva jvalan
english: Having routed all your troops, that best of men, Abhimanyu, stood, O king, blazing like a smokeless fire.

sanskrit: na cainaṃ tāvakāḥ sarve viṣehur arighātinam pradīptaṃ pāvakaṃ yadvat pataṃgāḥ kālacoditāḥ
english: And all your warriors could no more endure that slayer of foes than moths, driven by their doom, can endure a blazing fire.

sanskrit: praharan sarvaśatrubhyaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathaḥ adṛśyata maheṣvāsaḥ savajra iva vajrabhṛt
english: Striking down all his foes, that great archer and mighty warrior of the Pāṇḍavas appeared like the Thunderbolt-bearer with his thunderbolt in hand.

sanskrit: hemapṛṣṭhaṃ dhanuś cāsya dadṛśe carato diśaḥ toyadeṣu yathā rājan bhrājamānāḥ śatahvadāḥ
english: His gold-backed bow was seen, as he ranged through the quarters, gleaming like flashes of lightning amid the rainclouds, O king.

sanskrit: śarāś ca niśitāḥ pītā niścaranti sma saṃyuge vanāt phulladrumād rājan bhramarāṇām iva vrajāḥ
english: And his sharp, keen-whetted shafts darted forth in the battle, O king, like swarms of bees from a forest of trees in full bloom.

sanskrit: tathaiva caratas tasya saubhadrasya mahātmanaḥ rathena meghaghoṣeṇa dadṛśur nāntaraṃ janāḥ
english: As that high-souled son of Subhadrā ranged about thus, upon his thunder-roaring chariot, men could discern no interval in his action.

sanskrit: mohayitvā kṛpaṃ droṇaṃ drauṇiṃ ca sa bṛhadbalam saindhavaṃ ca maheṣvāsaṃ vyacaral laghu suṣṭhu ca
english: Bewildering Kṛpa and Droṇa, and Droṇa's son, and Bṛhadbala, and the great archer who was lord of the Sindhus, he ranged about lightly and well.

sanskrit: maṇḍalīkṛtam evāsya dhanuḥ paśyāma māriṣa sūryamaṇḍalasaṃkāśaṃ tapatas tava vāhinīm
english: We beheld his bow drawn ever into a circle, O venerable one, resembling the orb of the sun, as he scorched your host.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣatriyāḥ śūrāḥ pratapantaṃ śarārcibhiḥ dviphalgunam imaṃ lokaṃ menire tasya karmabhiḥ
english: Beholding him scorching all with the flames of his arrows, the heroic Kṣatriyas, from his deeds, deemed this world to have two Phalgunas.

sanskrit: tenārditā mahārāja bhāratī sā mahācamūḥ babhrāma tatra tatraiva yoṣin madavaśād iva
english: Tormented by him, O great king, that great army of the Bhāratas reeled this way and that, like a woman in the grip of drink.
